title: Inspect the protected utility drivetrain
summary: Check chain guard clearance, the visible chain/sprocket path and internal-hub shifting without opening the hub.

steps.title: Inspect the chain guard first
steps.instruction: Check the chain guard for cracks, loose mounts, rubbing or deformation that could contact the crank, chainring, chain or rear wheel.
steps.why: The guard is protective only while it remains clear of the moving drivetrain.
steps.warning: Do not ride if the chain guard is loose enough to contact the drivetrain or wheel.
steps.check: The guard appears secure and clear of moving parts.

steps.title: Inspect the visible chain and sprocket path
steps.instruction: Where visible and accessible without disassembly, look for obvious rust, damaged links, severe contamination, damaged sprocket teeth or abnormal chain alignment.
steps.why: Internal gearing reduces exposed shifting hardware, but the external chain drive still wears and needs inspection.
steps.warning: Keep fingers, cloth and loose clothing away from the drivetrain while the cranks or wheel are moving.
steps.check: No obvious external drivetrain damage or unsafe interference is visible.

steps.title: Check gear selection through the available range
steps.instruction: Using the hub manufacturer's permitted shifting method, operate the shifter through the available gears during a controlled check and note missed engagement, unusual resistance or persistent noise.
steps.why: Shift behavior can reveal cable/control adjustment or hub-system problems without opening the mechanism.
steps.warning: Different internal-gear hubs have different rules for shifting under load or while stationary. Follow the actual hub instructions.
steps.check: The hub selects gears predictably according to its own operating instructions.

steps.title: Stop at the internal-service boundary
steps.instruction: If symptoms point inside the hub, use the exact hub model's service documentation or qualified service rather than applying a generic Bike Atlas teardown.
steps.why: Internal-gear hubs differ in lubrication, adjustment, tooling and service intervals.
steps.warning: Do not open, flush, lubricate or adjust the hub internally using instructions for a different hub design.
steps.check: Any unresolved internal symptom is routed to the correct model-specific service procedure.
